stem: Root-zone EC is higher than feed EC. What can be concluded from EC alone?
choices: The root zone has a higher total dissolved-ion concentration, but EC alone does not identify which ions caused it
A specific nutrient is probably excessive because individual nutrient concentrations can usually be inferred from the size of the EC increase
The root zone is likely too dry because higher EC is primarily a direct measurement of root-zone water content
The pH meter should be recalibrated because disagreement between feed and root-zone EC usually indicates a pH-instrument error
rationale: EC reflects total ionic conductivity. It can show concentration differences but is not a nutrient-specific assay.
